reason: The passage emphasizes hierarchy through multiple layers: divine authority (God/Yahweh) at the apex, human leadership (Moses for Israel, Pharaoh for Egypt) in the middle, and subordinate populations below. The narrative structure is built around hierarchical relationships of command and obedience - Pharaoh directs his servants and military forces, Moses gives instructions to the Israelites who listen and follow, and God communicates His will through Moses as His agent. The text presents this structured chain of command as the operative framework for both Egyptian and Israelite societies.
